acceptance: Hub and CLI report channel, support state, and required update without ambiguity.
verifiedBy: node --test tests/compat/release-channel-compatibility.test.mjs (14/14 pass, executed -- see commands.log). node scripts/release/verify-release-plan.mjs --task MBR-912 (the manifest command) was not run; per MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md the manifest commands list runs once at the final phased book gate, not per task.
observed: release/channels/release-channel.v1.schema.json (pre-existing) and engine/crates/membrane-protocol/src/release_channel.rs's ReleaseChannelV1 (pre-existing) define the unambiguous shape: channel is one of exactly stable/beta/nightly; support.state is one of exactly supported/degraded/unsupported/unknown with an explicit startsAt/endsAt window; schemaCompatibility is one of exactly compatible/migration_required/incompatible/unknown; signedUpdateEvidence is either a non-empty string or null, and null is defined as 'unavailable', never an implicit update. This task adds the part that was missing for 'without ambiguity' to be a real guarantee rather than a shape description: engine/crates/membrane-protocol/src/compatibility_policy.rs's evaluate_compatibility/evaluate_release_channel and its dependency-free JS mirror release/channels/compatibility-policy.mjs's evaluateCompatibility/evaluateReleaseChannel. Both take a candidate release plus the locally installed version and return either an unambiguous admit (typed channel + release + migrationRequired flag) or an unambiguous refuse (every violation collected, each with a stable machine-checkable code: release_channel_unknown, release_channel_schema_version_unsupported, release_channel_schema_compatibility_unknown, release_channel_schema_incompatible, release_channel_downgrade_rejected, release_channel_version_unparseable). Fail-closed is proven, not asserted: 14 executed JS tests (node --test, all passing) cover an unknown channel, an unsupported schema version, an unrecognized or explicit 'unknown' schemaCompatibility, an incompatible schema, a downgrade, an equal version, an unparseable candidate or current version, and a case with four simultaneous violations all collected together -- none of these admit by default. The downgrade rule is bound to membrane-updater's (MBR-911) own downgrade rejection by using the identical strictly-greater major.minor.patch comparison, so this policy and the update-signature admission gate cannot disagree about what counts as an upgrade.
gap: This task adds the enforcement functions and proves them fail-closed with executable tests; it does not itself wire a Hub or CLI UI call site to invoke them before rendering a channel/support/required-update decision on screen. apps/membrane-hub/** is outside this task's allowed paths (this task's explicit owner instructions restrict it to release/channels/**, engine/crates/membrane-protocol/**, docs/compatibility/**, tests/compat/**, evidence/productization/MBR-912/**, overriding the more permissive apps/membrane-hub/** entry in dispatch-manifest.json's allowedPaths for MBR-912); apps/membrane-hub/src/release-channel.mjs (landed by the prior MBR-912 partial commit 62c29923) is a pure read-only projection/renderer today and does not call this task's new policy. release/channels/README.md and docs/compatibility/release-channels.md both name this gap explicitly. The Rust side's #[test]s are source-verified by type, not executed, per this task's no-cargo hard rule; they run at the Book 3 final phased gate (cargo test --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --workspace) alongside MBR-903's and MBR-911's own #[test] blocks. Per this task's instructions this is reported, not silently deferred: acceptanceStatus/status stay pending_book_gate and the manifest command node scripts/release/verify-release-plan.mjs --task MBR-912 was not executed here.
